title: Private jet charter in Europe: airports, slots and rules
description: Private flights in Europe: how airport hours, permission systems and the EU cabotage rule shape a trip, with guides to London, Geneva, Nice and Paris.
lead: Europe has many airports used by private jets, with strict local rules on hours, noise and permission. What to know before you plan a trip, and our city and airport guides.

sections.h: Hours and night rules differ by airport
p: In Europe, the biggest difference between airports is often the opening hours. Farnborough near London is {{eglf.hours}}. At Paris–Le Bourget, {{lfpb.curfew}}. At Geneva, {{lsgg.curfew}}.

Inside the European Union, flights between EU airports are intra-Community air services, and {{cab.eu}} ({{cab.eu.ref}}). In practice, an operator from outside the EU cannot normally operate a flight between two EU airports. We check the operator's licence against every leg before you see a quote. Our cabotage guide explains the rules.

Many European airports manage private flights through slots or permission. At Geneva, {{lsgg.ppr}}. Nice is {{lfmn.slots}}. Others are simpler: at Biggin Hill near London, {{egkb.slots}}, and Paris–Le Bourget is {{lfpb.slots}}.
Our city guides cover London, Geneva, Paris, and Nice with Cannes. Our airport guide covers Farnborough. More cities follow, each checked against official sources before it is published.

We are a broker, not an airline, and we have no fixed routes. Tell us where you want to go and when, and we find aircraft from licensed operators, check each operator and name it in your quote before you confirm. Any aircraft, any route, upon availability.
